How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Pricing

Pricing is usually not public. This states what is known, what is estimated, and what is not public.

Pricing
KnownNo list prices are published. The Product Guide says pricing depends on the platform tier (Core or Advanced), the user band and the number of exercising credits, and that use above the band or the credits may be charged at then-current rates.; One technical exercising credit covers one team of up to 10 users in one cyber range or Dynamic Threat Range exercise; one business credit covers one Crisis Simulation with no limit on participants. Credits are allocated per subscription year and do not roll over.; The Master Services Agreement allows fees to be changed at renewal with notice before the term ends. Premium support is sold under a separate statement of work. Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. Has any Immersive Labs group company been subject to a regulatory investigation, enforcement action, fine or order in any jurisdiction, including by a data protection authority?
    Regulatory action against a supplier is a factor in third-party risk assessment.
  2. Is any Immersive Labs group company party to material litigation or arbitration, as claimant or defendant?
    Material litigation can affect a supplier's finances and its ability to deliver.
  3. Has Immersive had a security incident or personal data breach affecting customer or end-user data in the last five years, and how were customers told?
    A supplier's own incident record indicates how well it protects customer data.
  4. Which enterprise or government customers have not renewed in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of major customers can signal product or service problems.
  5. Have there been any departures of senior executives in the last 24 months for reasons of conduct or dispute, and what was the reason for the change of chief executive in March 2025?
    Leadership instability or misconduct can affect delivery and governance.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-18 · launch Immersive
    Immersive announces Immersive AI Security in early access

    On 18 November 2026 the company announced a new product family, Immersive AI Security, with two products: AI Govern & Control, which monitors and controls how staff use AI tools in the browser, and AI Observe & Assess, an on-premises appliance that maps and tests internally built AI agents. Both link findings to training in Immersive One. They are in an early-access programme, with general availability planned for early 2027. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-23, opens in new tab)Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-23, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-03-17 · launch Immersive
    Immersive One adds AI security labs, vendor-specific exercises and framework heat maps

    On 17 March 2026 the company announced additions to Immersive One: hands-on labs on agentic AI and prompt injection, exercises using CrowdStrike Falcon, Google Security Operations, Splunk, IBM QRadar and Microsoft Sentinel, enhanced after-action reporting for crisis simulations, and heat maps aligned to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST NICE and MITRE frameworks. No availability date was given. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  3. 2025-11-19 · launch Immersive
    Immersive launches Dynamic Threat Range for live-fire team exercises

    The company announced general availability of Dynamic Threat Range within Immersive One on 19 November 2025. The release says it runs full attack chains in supported enterprise environments, initially with Elastic and Splunk, and measures time to detect and respond. Microsoft Sentinel support and custom exercise creation were described as planned for early 2026. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-23, opens in new tab)

  4. 2025-09-16 · leadership change Immersive
    Immersive appoints a chief product officer and a chief technology officer

    On 16 September 2025 the company named Aniket Menon, formerly a vice-president of product at Rapid7, as chief product officer and confirmed Thanos Karpouzis, previously its vice-president of engineering, as chief technology officer. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  5. 2025-09-11 · partnership ImmersiveCycode
    Immersive and Cycode announce a partnership on secure software development

    In a release dated 11 September 2025 the two companies said they would combine Immersive's developer security training with Cycode's code scanning results, so that findings can direct targeted training. The combined offering was described as due in the following months. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  6. 2025-03-11 · leadership change Immersive
    Immersive names Mark Schmitz chief executive; founder James Hadley becomes chief innovation officer

    The company announced on 11 March 2025 that Mark Schmitz, previously president of Collibra and interim chief executive of Citrix, would join as chief executive on 17 March 2025. Founder James Hadley moved to chief innovation officer and stayed on the board. BusinessCloud reported the appointment the next day, and the group's 2025 accounts record the change. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-23, opens in new tab)BusinessCloud (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)Companies House (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  7. 2025-02-12 · rebrand Immersive
    Immersive Labs renames itself Immersive and its platform Immersive One

    On 12 February 2025 the company announced that it was dropping Labs from its trading name and renaming its platform Immersive One, which it described as a single platform of hands-on labs, simulations, cyber drills and ranges for technical and non-technical staff. The legal entities kept the Immersive Labs name. Immersive (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)
